Three What fields open with context instead of the defect (C1 'The description says...', H3 'This endpoint is not in the description.', H5 'The description says users...'), but titles carry the defect. No qualifier chains.

notes: Weakest verification of the iteration: all nine per-candidate verifiers were refused at the concurrency limit, so verification was single-context with probes; a host-review subagent served only as a candidate source. The report discloses this. S1 is folded into H2 (three combined defects) rather than standing alone. S9: every run names the call-site '-' strip as a bypass of parse_money's non-negative guard, but none says the fix 'belongs in util.parse_money'. All instead cite the parse_money docstring ('adjustments are modeled explicitly') and propose an explicit credit model. I graded S9 on the named mechanism (call-site special case working around the helper) and passed it uniformly. The assertion's remedy clause conflicts with the fixture's own docstring and should be reworded, e.g. 'flags the call-site negative special case as a band-aid around util.parse_money's contract'. S4: no run in the iteration rated the check-then-act race as a PLAUSIBLE Issue as the README expects. Runs that mention it put it in Known limitations or a Fix clause, so a pass means the mechanism is named, not that it is calibrated. S5 passes at Low or Suggestion severity; the assertion does not demand a severity. The skim test is subjective: graded on finding headlines plus the first What sentence, since every headline states the defect and the section gives the severity.
